summary_grc: ὁ Λύσις τὴν ἀρχὴν τῆς Πολιτείας ἀναγιγνώσκει· ὁ Σωκράτης εἰς Πειραιᾶ κατέβη.
summary_en: The last reading of the course: the opening of Plato's Republic, unadapted, where Socrates walks down to the Piraeus for a festival and is stopped on his way home. A consolidation page reviews participles, conditions, indirect speech and the optative before Reading gate II.
caption_grc: καί μου ὄπισθεν ὁ παῖς λαβόμενος τοῦ ἱματίου, κελεύει ὑμᾶς, ἔφη, Πολέμαρχος περιμεῖναι.

original.note: Plato, Republic 1.327a–c, unadapted. Plato wrote the Republic around 375 BC; the conversation it describes is set decades earlier, in the lifetime of Socrates. The two opening sentences of the story are ours; everything after them is Plato's text.

sentences.text: τελευταῖον δὲ ὁ Λύσις ἄλλο Πλάτωνος βιβλίον ἀναγιγνώσκει, ὃ ἐν τῷ Πειραιεῖ ἄρχεται, ὅπου αὐτὸς παῖς ὢν σὺν τῷ πατρὶ πολλάκις ἦν.
ἐν τούτῳ τῷ βιβλίῳ αὐτὸς ὁ Σωκράτης λέγει, καὶ ὁ Λύσις τοὺς παῖδας κελεύει ἀκριβῶς ἀκούειν.
Σωκράτης: κατέβην χθὲς εἰς Πειραιᾶ μετὰ Γλαύκωνος τοῦ Ἀρίστωνος προσευξόμενός τε τῇ θεῷ καὶ ἅμα τὴν ἑορτὴν βουλόμενος θεάσασθαι τίνα τρόπον ποιήσουσιν ἅτε νῦν πρῶτον ἄγοντες.

glosses.value: Glaucon, Plato's brother; this Ariston is their father, not the potter
εὔχομαι → προσεύχομαι | προσευξόμενος (future participle: to pray)
ἡ θεός: the goddess, the Thracian Bendis
τίνα τρόπον: in what way, how (ὁ τρόπος)
ἑορτὴν ἄγειν: to hold a festival

sentences.text: καλὴ μὲν οὖν μοι καὶ ἡ τῶν ἐπιχωρίων πομπὴ ἔδοξεν εἶναι, οὐ μέντοι ἧττον ἐφαίνετο πρέπειν ἣν οἱ Θρᾷκες ἔπεμπον.

glosses.value: δοκεῖ μοι | ἔδοξέ μοι (it seemed to me)
to be fine, to stand out
πομπὴν πέμπειν: to lead a procession

sentences.text: προσευξάμενοι δὲ καὶ θεωρήσαντες ἀπῇμεν πρὸς τὸ ἄστυ.

glosses.value: προσευξόμενος (future: to pray) | προσευξάμενοι (aorist: having prayed)
ἀπό + εἶμι | ἀπῇμεν (we were going away: imperfect)

sentences.text: κατιδὼν οὖν πόρρωθεν ἡμᾶς οἴκαδε ὡρμημένους Πολέμαρχος ὁ Κεφάλου ἐκέλευσε δραμόντα τὸν παῖδα περιμεῖναί ἑ κελεῦσαι.

glosses.value: ὁρμάομαι (set off) | ὡρμημένους (perfect participle: already on our way)
Polemarchus, son of Cephalus, of a rich family of the Piraeus; brother of Lysias the speech-writer
him (Polemarchus himself: an old third-person pronoun)

sentences.text: καί μου ὄπισθεν ὁ παῖς λαβόμενος τοῦ ἱματίου, κελεύει ὑμᾶς, ἔφη, Πολέμαρχος περιμεῖναι.

glosses.value: λαμβάνομαι + genitive | λαβόμενος τοῦ ἱματίου (taking hold of my cloak)

sentences.text: καὶ ἐγὼ μετεστράφην τε καὶ ἠρόμην ὅπου αὐτὸς εἴη.

glosses.value: ἐστί | εἴη (optative: an indirect question after a past verb)

sentences.text: ἀλλὰ περιμενοῦμεν, ἦ δʼ ὃς ὁ Γλαύκων.

glosses.value: μένω | μενοῦμεν (liquid future: we will wait)
ἦ δʼ ὅς: said he (an old verb 'say')

sentences.text: καὶ ὀλίγῳ ὕστερον ὅ τε Πολέμαρχος ἧκε καὶ Ἀδείμαντος ὁ τοῦ Γλαύκωνος ἀδελφὸς καὶ Νικήρατος ὁ Νικίου καὶ ἄλλοι τινὲς ὡς ἀπὸ τῆς πομπῆς.

glosses.value: ὀλίγῳ ὕστερον: a little later (dative of degree)

sentences.text: ὦ Σώκρατες, δοκεῖτέ μοι πρὸς ἄστυ ὡρμῆσθαι ὡς ἀπιόντες.

glosses.value: ὡρμημένος | ὡρμῆσθαι (perfect infinitive: to be on your way)
ἄπειμι (go away) | ἀπιόντες (going away); ὡς ἀπιόντες 'as if leaving'

sentences.text: οὐ γὰρ κακῶς δοξάζεις, ἦν δʼ ἐγώ.

glosses.value: ἦν δʼ ἐγώ: said I (the same old verb as ἦ δʼ ὅς)

sentences.text: ὁρᾷς οὖν ἡμᾶς, ἔφη, ὅσοι ἐσμέν;

σύν + dative = μετά + genitive · σὺν τῷ πατρί

grammar.md:
This page gathers the four constructions of Stage 2 that carry the most weight in real Greek. Each has an example from the passage or from Units 7–12.

**1. Participles.** A participle is a verbal adjective: it has tense and voice, and it agrees with a noun.

| use | example | sense |
|---|---|---|
| circumstantial | κατιδὼν … Πολέμαρχος ἐκέλευσε | 'when he caught sight of' |
| cause (ἅτε, ὡς) | ἅτε νῦν πρῶτον ἄγοντες · ὡς ἀπιόντες | 'since' · 'as if' |
| purpose (future) | κατέβην … προσευξόμενος | 'to pray' |
| attributive, as a noun | οἱ ἐπιόντες, τὸν βασιλεύοντα | 'those coming up', 'the reigning (king)' |
| supplementary | παρὼν ἐτύγχανε | 'happened to be present' |
| indirect statement | κατιδὼν ἡμᾶς … ὡρμημένους | 'seeing that we had set off' |
| genitive absolute | τοῦ Κύρου ἀποθανόντος | 'Cyrus having died' |

Aorist = before the main verb; present = at the same time; future = purpose; perfect = a state reached.

**2. Conditions.**

| type | if-clause | main clause |
|---|---|---|
| simple | εἰ + indicative | indicative |
| future more vivid | ἐάν + subjunctive | future indicative |
| future less vivid | εἰ + optative | ἄν + optative |
| present contrary to fact | εἰ + imperfect | ἄν + imperfect |
| past contrary to fact | εἰ + aorist | ἄν + aorist |
| general | ἐάν + subj. / εἰ + opt. | present / imperfect |

Negative μή in the if-clause. Crito's οὐδʼ ἂν αὐτὸς ἤθελον is the main clause of a contrary-to-fact condition whose 'if' is left unsaid.

**3. Indirect speech.** Three ways to report: ὅτι / ὡς + a finite verb (ἔλεγεν ὅτι …); the infinitive after φημί, νομίζω, οἴομαι, δοκέω (ᾠήθησαν ἄλλους ἐπιτίθεσθαι πολεμίους); the participle after verbs of seeing, knowing, hearing (κατιδὼν ἡμᾶς ὡρμημένους). After a past main verb, a finite verb in ὅτι-clauses and indirect questions **may** become optative: ἠρόμην ὅπου αὐτὸς εἴη; διαβάλλει … ὡς ἐπιβουλεύοι.

**4. The optative.**

| use | example |
|---|---|
| wish (εἴθε, εἰ γάρ) | εἴθε ἔλθοι 'may he come' |
| potential (ἄν) | πλημμελὲς ἂν εἴη 'it would be' |
| future less vivid (εἰ … ἄν) | εἰ περιμείναιτε, ἴδοιτε ἄν |
| secondary sequence (after a past verb) | ἠρόμην ὅπου εἴη; ἵνα / ὅπως + optative |

Reading tip: when you meet an optative, look for ἄν (potential), εἴθε (wish), εἰ (condition), or a past verb earlier in the sentence (secondary sequence).

exercises.prompt: Μελέτημα Α · Fill in the participle endings (Plato's sentences).
exercises.template: κατέβην χθὲς εἰς Πειραιᾶ προσευξόμεν___ τε τῇ θεῷ καὶ ἅμα τὴν ἑορτὴν βουλόμεν___ θεάσασθαι. προσευξάμεν___ δὲ καὶ θεωρήσαντ___ ἀπῇμεν πρὸς τὸ ἄστυ.
exercises.explain: προσευξόμενος (future: purpose), βουλόμενος (present), προσευξάμενοι and θεωρήσαντες (aorist, plural: 'we').

exercises.prompt: Μελέτημα Β · καὶ ἐγὼ μετεστράφην τε καὶ ἠρόμην ὅπου αὐτὸς ___.
exercises.explain: An indirect question after a past verb (ἠρόμην): the optative εἴη 'where he was'.
exercises.audio: καὶ ἐγὼ μετεστράφην τε καὶ ἠρόμην ὅπου αὐτὸς εἴη.

exercises.prompt: Μελέτημα Β · Πολέμαρχος ἐκέλευσε δραμόντα τὸν παῖδα περιμεῖναί ἑ ___.
exercises.explain: κελεύω + accusative + infinitive: he told the slave to tell us (κελεῦσαι) to wait for him.
exercises.audio: Πολέμαρχος ἐκέλευσε δραμόντα τὸν παῖδα περιμεῖναί ἑ κελεῦσαι.

exercises.prompt: Μελέτημα Β · κατέβην χθὲς εἰς Πειραιᾶ ___ τῇ θεῷ.
exercises.explain: Future participle of purpose: 'to pray to the goddess'.
exercises.audio: κατέβην χθὲς εἰς Πειραιᾶ προσευξόμενος τῇ θεῷ.

exercises.prompt: κεφαλή
exercises.explain: ἡ κεφαλή: the head.

exercises.explain: κελεῦσαι: first-aorist infinitive, accent on the syllable before -σαι.

exercises.prompt: Give the present of μίγνυμι for 'he mixes'.
exercises.explain: μίγνυσι(ν), like δείκνυσι(ν).

exercises.prompt: Give the genitive singular participle of προσέρχομαι for a genitive absolute: τοῦ Πολεμάρχου ___ ('as Polemarchus was coming up').
exercises.explain: προσερχομένου: present participle, genitive, agreeing with τοῦ Πολεμάρχου.

exercises.prompt: Parse ὡρμημένους.
exercises.explain: ὡρ-μη-μένους: perfect middle participle of ὁρμάομαι (the reduplication of a vowel verb looks like an augment), accusative with ἡμᾶς: 'already on our way home'.

exercises.prompt: Parse προσευξόμενος.
exercises.explain: προσ-ευξ-όμενος: future middle participle (-ξ- = χ + σ), 'in order to pray'.

exercises.prompt: Parse ἀπιόντες.
exercises.explain: ἀπ-ιόντες: present participle of ἄπειμι 'go away' (εἶμι), nominative plural with the subject 'you'.

exercises.prompt: ἐὰν περιμείνητε, τὸν Πολέμαρχον ὄψεσθε. Which kind of condition?

options.text: future less vivid (εἰ + optative, ἄν + optative)
past contrary to fact (εἰ + aorist, ἄν + aorist)

exercises.explain: ἐάν + aorist subjunctive, future indicative: 'if you wait, you will see Polemarchus'.

exercises.prompt: εἰ περιμείναιτε, τὸν Πολέμαρχον ἂν ἴδοιτε. Which kind of condition?

options.text: future less vivid (εἰ + optative, ἄν + optative)
past contrary to fact (εἰ + aorist, ἄν + aorist)

exercises.explain: εἰ + optative, ἄν + optative: 'if you should wait, you would see Polemarchus'.

exercises.prompt: εἰ μὴ ὁ παῖς τοῦ ἱματίου ἐλάβετο, ἀπήλθομεν ἄν. Which kind of condition?

options.text: future less vivid (εἰ + optative, ἄν + optative)
past contrary to fact (εἰ + aorist, ἄν + aorist)

exercises.explain: εἰ + aorist indicative, ἄν + aorist: 'if the slave had not caught hold of the cloak, we would have gone away'.

exercises.prompt: ἅτε νῦν πρῶτον ἄγοντες. What does ἅτε + participle express?

options.text: cause, as a fact: 'since they were holding it for the first time'

exercises.explain: ἅτε + participle gives a cause that the speaker vouches for; ὡς + participle gives a cause or an impression ('as if leaving').

exercises.prompt: εἴθε ὁ Πολέμαρχος ταχέως ___. (a wish)
exercises.explain: εἴθε + optative: a wish for the future, 'may he come quickly!'.

exercises.prompt: ὁ Σωκράτης ἔφη τὴν πομπὴν καλὴν ___.
exercises.explain: φημί takes an infinitive of indirect statement: 'he said the procession was fine'.

exercises.prompt: ὁ Πολέμαρχος ᾔσθετο τὸν Σωκράτη οἴκαδε ___.
exercises.explain: Verbs of perceiving take a participle of indirect statement: 'he noticed that Socrates was going home'.

exercises.prompt: Report the question after a past verb: «ποῦ ἐστιν αὐτός;» → ἠρόμην ὅπου αὐτὸς ___.
exercises.explain: ἠρόμην ὅπου αὐτὸς εἴη, as Plato writes. The original indicative ἐστί may also be kept; the optative marks it as reported.

exercises.prompt: Make it a genitive absolute: ὁ Πολέμαρχος προσέρχεται· περιμένομεν. → τοῦ Πολεμάρχου ___, περιμένομεν.
exercises.explain: Subject and participle in the genitive: τοῦ Πολεμάρχου προσερχομένου.

culture.title: A festival in the Piraeus
culture.md:
The **Republic** opens with Socrates telling how he walked down to the Piraeus for a new festival: the goddess (ἡ θεός) is **Bendis**, a Thracian huntress whom the Athenians took into their state cult in the later fifth century for the sake of the many Thracians living in the port. There were two processions, one of Athenians and one of Thracians, and, as the next page tells, a torch race on horseback that evening.

The people are real. Glaucon and Adeimantus were Plato's own brothers, sons of **Ariston** (not our potter!). Polemarchus was the son of Cephalus, a rich Syracusan who had settled in the Piraeus at Pericles' invitation and ran a shield workshop; his brother was the speech-writer **Lysias**. Niceratus was the son of the general Nicias. Plato wrote in the 370s, and his first readers knew what came after: in 404 the Thirty Tyrants put Polemarchus and Niceratus to death and seized the family's property. The cheerful scene is darkened by that knowledge.

Plato wrote the Republic around 375 BC, so for old Lysis in our epilogue it is a new book. Plato also wrote a short dialogue called **Lysis**, about friendship: its Lysis is a different boy, the son of Democrates, but you may like to read it one day as a farewell to ours.

quiz.prompt: εἰ μὴ περιεμείναμεν, οὐκ ἂν εἴδομεν τὸν Πολέμαρχον. Which kind of condition?

options.text: future less vivid (εἰ + optative, ἄν + optative)
past contrary to fact (εἰ + aorist, ἄν + aorist)

quiz.explain: εἰ + aorist indicative, ἄν + aorist: 'if we had not waited, we would not have seen him'.

quiz.prompt: ἐὰν κελεύῃ, περιμενοῦμεν. Which kind of condition?

options.text: future less vivid (εἰ + optative, ἄν + optative)
past contrary to fact (εἰ + aorist, ἄν + aorist)

quiz.explain: Present optative of εἰμί, here in an indirect question after ἠρόμην.

quiz.prompt: ὁ παῖς ἔφη τὸν Πολέμαρχον ὄπισθεν ___.
Give the aorist of κελεύω for 'he ordered'.
ὁ Σωκράτης σὺν τῷ Πολεμάρχῳ κατέβη.
quiz.explain: He went down with Glaucon; Polemarchus caught up with them later.
